# Munch

> Munch is a privacy-conscious, MCP-first nutrition and cooking-history service. Your AI assistant — ChatGPT, Claude, or any other MCP client — provides the conversation and reasoning; Munch provides persistent nutrition records, independent cooking-session history with durable photos and timelines, verified food search, saved foods, immutable reusable recipes, goals, water and weight history, trends, exports, deletion, billing entitlements, and OAuth-protected MCP tools.

Munch is designed for use through ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP clients, with the Munch website as the structured home for logging, history, recipes, and billing rather than as a standalone nutrition application. Users can describe meals and cooking sessions naturally, attach cooking photos, record editable timelines and results, search history across conversations, repeat and compare attempts, search USDA FoodData Central and Open Food Facts, look up barcodes, save single foods or multi-ingredient recipes, log exact recipe servings with historical source snapshots, review daily progress and longer-term trends, and manage their account through conversation.

## Cooking sessions

- Cooks are persistent records independent of recipes, nutrition logs, and pantry deductions.
- A cook can contain multiple dishes, recipe-revision links, actual ingredients, deviations, original messages, durable photos, timeline events, results, and next-time notes.
- Users can start, update, finish, reopen, correct, delete, search, compare, repeat, and save a reviewed cook as a recipe through the Cooks website surface and MCP tools.
- Completing a cook does not imply that food was eaten or that pantry inventory was used. Those are separate, explicit actions.

Munch does not train a Munch model on nutrition records, sell nutrition data, or use Google Analytics or advertising trackers. Your AI provider separately controls its conversation processing, retention, and training choices according to your plan, settings, and the provider's policies.

## Connect Munch to your AI

Munch connects to any MCP client as a custom connector / remote MCP server. Full step-by-step instructions live at https://munch.business/connect — the summary:

- Endpoint: https://munch.business/mcp
- Connector name: Munch
- Authentication: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + DCR. Starting the connection opens a Munch page in the user's browser.
- Sign-in is by single-use email link — there is no password. Entering an email and opening the link Munch sends signs the user in; if the email has never been used with Munch, that same link creates the account automatically. There is no separate sign-up step. After sign-in, the user reviews the requested permissions on Munch's approval page and approves; the client is then connected.
- A returning user can also paste the connect block from https://munch.business/ into their AI chat and let the assistant walk them through the same steps.

Per-client summary:

- Claude: Customize → Connectors (Settings → Connectors in some versions) → + → Add custom connector → name Munch, URL https://munch.business/mcp → Add → Connect → complete the email-link sign-in and approval in the browser. Custom connectors are available on Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans; free accounts can keep one custom connector.
- ChatGPT: on the web, Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → turn on Developer mode → back in Apps & Connectors choose Create → name Munch, MCP server URL https://munch.business/mcp, Authentication OAuth → Create → complete the email-link sign-in and approval in the browser. Developer mode is a paid-plan feature (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu) and is not available on free accounts.
- Muse: run `claude mcp add --transport http Munch https://munch.business/mcp`, then run `/mcp`, choose Munch, and Authenticate; complete the email-link sign-in and approval in the browser.
- Any MCP app: open the app's custom connector / MCP server settings, add a server named Munch with URL https://munch.business/mcp and OAuth authentication, start the connection, and complete the email-link sign-in and approval in the browser.

After connecting, the assistant can confirm the connection is live and offer a first action — log a first meal or set a nutrition goal. Connections can be revoked at any time from Munch Settings → Connections; revoking stops that connection without deleting the account or its records. Support: support@munch.business.

## Access and billing

- Munch has a permanent Free tier for core nutrition logging, daily progress, water and weight tracking, imports, exports, connections, and account deletion.
- Optional Premium capabilities are managed on the Munch website. Connecting an MCP client does not require a subscription prompt or payment.
- Premium is $2.99/month for the owner. Additional household members are $2/month each after they accept an invitation; invitations are free until accepted.
- Checkout, recurring billing, payment methods, invoices, and cancellation are handled through Stripe on the website.

## Nutrition sources

Munch prioritizes structured sources and confirmed history:

1. USDA FoodData Central
2. Open Food Facts and barcode records
3. User-confirmed saved foods and prior meals
4. AI-assisted estimates when stronger structured data is unavailable

Sources and assumptions should remain visible. Munch is a consumer wellness product and does not provide medical advice.

## Open-source attribution

Munch began as a fork of the MIT-licensed Nutrition MCP project by Alexander Kutishevsky. Munch preserves the original license and attribution while operating as an independent hosted product.
